author: Neema Parvini
body_text:
might we view the shape of history? Are there viable
alternatives to progressivism and, if so, what are
they? What impact does conceptualising history
in a distinctly ‘non-progressive’ way have? In every
age, there have been thinkers who might broadly
be described as Prophets of Doom. This does not
necessarily mean that they are pessimists, but rather
that they reject the notion that history is an inexorable
march of improvement. History is not, in their view,
a line on the graph going up and up ‘to infinity and
beyond’, but a recurring pattern of rise and fall.
